change.title: pr-3-flat
change.description: feat(upsampling) - Support upsampled error count with performance optimizations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Negated query `!event.type:error` counts as error-focused
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a plain substring check, so `!event.type:error` (every event *except* errors), `event.type:errors_foo`, or `message:"event.type:error"` all return True. On the discover dataset this applies `sum(sample_weight)` to queries that are mostly transactions. Transactions have no sample weight, so their counts come back as 0 or wrong, and nothing tells the user. Parse the query with the event-search parser, or at least reject a negated term, before you treat it as error-focused.

findings.title: Hard-coded `as count` alias breaks `transformAliasToInputFormat=1`
findings.body: The rewritten column always carries the alias `count`. The response serializer looks the value up by `resolve_axis_column(query_columns[0], ...)` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization_events.py:65-78). That gives `count` by default, but it returns the original `count()` when `transformAliasToInputFormat=1` (line 75-76). For those requests on allowlisted projects, the series key no longer matches the result column, so the chart shows empty or zero buckets and no error is raised. One option is to alias to `resolve_axis_column(column, ...)` of the original column; another is to keep the original column name as the alias.

findings.title: 60s eligibility cache has no working invalidation
findings.body: The comment on lines 50-53 says the allowlist is read fresh each time, but the result is cached for 60 seconds. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere: the option system has no hook that calls it, and it would need every org/project-set combination to work anyway. So after the allowlist changes, counts flip between upsampled and raw for up to a minute. A single `options.get` call is cheap, so you could drop the cache, or else remove the dead invalidator and correct the docstrings.

findings.title: What does `sum(sample_weight)` give for events without a sample weight?
findings.body: The comments say the schema guarantees `sample_weight` for every event in an allowlisted project. Events stored before the project was allowlisted, or sent by SDKs that set no client sample rate, may have a NULL `sample_weight`. `sum` skips NULLs, so those events would drop out of the count silently. Is there a default of 1 in the storage schema? If not, `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` would keep raw counts correct.

findings.title: Stray gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: This PR adds a submodule entry (`Subproject commit a5d2909...`), and the repository has no `.gitmodules`. It looks like an accidentally committed nested checkout, and it will confuse clones and CI. Remove it from the PR.

findings.title: Eligibility check uses `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`, and RPC branch is dead
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, which the dashboard split factory sets to `errors` when the request dataset is `discover`. The check still passes the outer `dataset`, so a split errors query only gets upsampled if the user's query literally contains `event.type:error`. Separately, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for spans_rpc and ourlogs, so the transform in the `use_rpc` branch (lines 275-277) never runs. The `should_upsample`/`upsampling_enabled` duplication and the comments about "query optimization" don't describe what the code does.

findings.title: Test creates the organization with `Organization.objects.create`
findings.body: CLAUDE.md (Common Gotchas #7) says to use the `self.create_*` helpers, not direct model creation. Use `self.create_organization(...)`.

findings.title: No test for negated queries or the cached path
findings.body: `test_is_error_focused_query` doesn't cover `!event.type:error`, which currently returns True. Nothing tests `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` itself, including its caching. The endpoint tests don't cover `transformAliasToInputFormat=1`, multiple yAxis values, or topEvents with upsampling.

contracts.action: Rewrite count() to upsampled_count() as count on events-stats for allowlisted error queries
contracts.equivalent_path: Unmodified timeseries_query/top_events_timeseries path with query_columns, then serialized by resolve_axis_column
contracts.before_after: Before: query_columns passed as-is. After: count() replaced by an aliased upsampled count when every project is allowlisted and the dataset/query is error-focused.
contracts.visible_effect: The serializer reads the value by get_function_alias('count()')='count', which matches the alias. With transformAliasToInputFormat=1 it reads 'count()', which doesn't match.
contracts.failure_mode: No new async calls. Cache read/write failures fall through to a fresh option check. A wrong eligibility decision (negated query) or an alias mismatch shows wrong counts with no error.

contracts.action: New SnQL function upsampled_count in the discover config, also used by the errors builder
contracts.equivalent_path: count() SnQL function in the same config
contracts.failure_mode: If sample_weight is NULL, those events silently drop out of the sum.
contracts.open_question: Does the storage schema default sample_weight to 1 for events without client sampling?

summary:
The PR adds error upsampling to events-stats by rewriting `count()` to `sum(sample_weight)`. I found three things to fix and five to consider, none blocking.

Fix:
- The error-focused check is a plain substring match, so `!event.type:error` also turns upsampling on.
- The `as count` alias doesn't match the series key when a request sends `transformAliasToInputFormat=1`, so those charts lose their data with no error.
- The PR commits a stray `sentry-repo` submodule entry, and the repository has no `.gitmodules`.

Consider:
- The 60-second eligibility cache can't be invalidated: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called.
- What `sum(sample_weight)` gives when an event has no sample weight is an open question.
- The eligibility check passes the outer `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`, and the transform in the RPC branch never runs.
- One test creates its organization directly, which CLAUDE.md rules out.
- Tests don't cover negated queries, the cached path, the alias flag, or topEvents.
